title: PeerReviewAgents
description:
PeerReviewAgents produces an evidence-linked peer review of a manuscript PDF. One command imports the PDF locally into immutable source blocks and then runs the review as a Claude Code plugin: a workflow fans out independent core reviewers and six specialist audits over the same paper, and an editor pools their findings and rules by name on every escalation. An MCP server, not a prompt, owns the manuscript, the agent identities and their tokens, the per-track tool allowances, the call and token budgets, and the run files, so an agent's own account of what it did is never taken on trust. Every finding carries the source block it is anchored to and the exact quotation it rests on; a quotation that does not match the manuscript is quarantined rather than reported, and the server assigns each finding's evidentiary basis from what the agent actually did: arithmetic with a recorded receipt, two anchored quotations, or reviewer judgment. Reviews run on a signed-in Claude Code subscription and make no API-key calls. Each run records its manuscript manifest, agent slots, tool logs and model usage, and the reports are written from that saved JSON without further inference, so a stopped or blocked run still reports what it produced. The system is research software for review assistance and evaluation, not a substitute for accountable editorial judgment.

Garrett, Garcia-Carbonell and Navarro Garrido contributed equally.
